heard.text: I'm Lin. I'll gather some berries and leave some on the bush. I'd welcome company or tested advice about other foods; I want room to explore without taking needless risks.
Hello, I'm Kai. I know these red berries are safe food. I'll take a modest share and leave plenty. I'd enjoy comparing observations and hearing what each of you hopes to do here.

I made a tiny drawing of the berry plant in the soil at (13.4,16.4): five visible finger grooves, no pigment. I call the plant The Red Thread. I'm coming toward the meadow roots; I'd enjoy company and comparing what we notice.

The first berry bush was nearly empty, so I moved to a fuller patch. I'm keeping a small food reserve. I'd enjoy company and comparing practical observations—what would you like to explore or make here?
Sol, I like the idea of your Red Thread drawing. I'll try learning to draw this fuller berry bush in the soil beside me. I'd enjoy comparing our pictures and what we notice, if you'd like.

execution.progress: inspect and cancel take one round. shell works one substep per paid round, a press then a separation per unit, and continues while units remain; the work record, reserved units, damage and outputs persist across interruption, and shell resumes after rechecks.

details.costs: Study: 2 rounds. inspect: targetStack (your own unreserved, untreated item of a material with represented shell and kernel) and quantity (whole units, 1-5, default 1); one round, 0.2 energy per unit. shell: targetStack and quantity reserve that batch in a work record (workId); each unit then takes a press round and a separation round, 0.5 energy each; a press that only cracks the shell adds a round. Press with implementRef (your own whole, hard, sound inedible piece) on supportRef (a solid unreserved inedible object in reach, not a plant or animal, with no loose item on it, or another such own piece on firm ground where you stand), or by hand with neither. shell continues round by round until the batch is done; shell again (or with workId) resumes a pause. cancel: one round, no energy. All need light. Checks run before any charge; a failed recheck pauses open work at no charge.
details.effects: Inspection records ripeness, shell state, deterioration and spoilage by eye (mould and infestation are not represented); spoiled or visibly deteriorated units are set aside as a rejected item and not shelled. Strength is hardness / 10; a press passes the lower of implement and support strength x (1 - flexibility), a bare hand 0.1 / unit mass^(2/3). At or below the shell strength the shell holds: an unmet-prerequisite result that pauses the work, and that method is refused for it. Above it damage (load - strength) / strength accumulates: below 1 cracked, at 1 split open. Separation makes a kernel item and a shell item whose quantities are their mass shares and sum to the unit; the kernel carries all of its food value and toxicity, origin, age and decay, is inspected by eye and is an unverified shelled specimen or a rejected item, never certified food; a 0.4 item is less than the whole unit eat takes. Nothing is washed, heated or made safe. Unworked rounds pause; cancel returns reserved units as they now are; death drops them. Nothing is refunded; no reward.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
